newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Renault workers head for Paris.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Renault workers head for Paris.

text.p: A convoy of workers from French carmaker Renault's condemned Belgian plant headed for Paris on Tuesday to take part in an international demonstration against the company's restructuring plans.

About 80 coaches carrying more than 3,000 people left the plant at Vilvoorde near Brussels at 0400 GMT in thick fog. It was due to arrive in Paris at 1000 GMT for the demonstration of workers from France, Belgium and Spain.

Organisers expect more than 10,000 people to take in the demonstration at Renault's headquarters at Boulogne-Billancourt on the outskirts of Paris against the firm's plans to axe some 6,000 jobs in Europe.
The protest is due to be held before a meeting between chairman Louis Schweitzer and Renault's European staff works council at 1300 GMT.

"We're going to ask for two things at the meeting -- that Renault reconsider the closure of the Vilvoorde plant, and for the start of negotiations to reduce working hours to preserve jobs under the (French) Robien law," Emmanuel Couvreur, a spokesman for the French CFDT union, said on Monday.
Renault announced on February 27 that it would close the Vilvoorde plant, which employs 3,100 people, in July as part of a programme to reorganise and streamline its European car assembly operations.
Last week it also announced plans to eliminate 2,764 jobs in France this year, up from 1,640 job cuts in 1996.
The moves have sparked an uproar not just among workers but also among French and Belgian politicians who say they are appalled by the brutality of the measures and the short notice.
